newsitem.title: UK: EU's Brittan challenges Conservative Eurosceptics.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan challenges Conservative Eurosceptics.

text.p: Sir Leon Brittan, the British Conservative member of the European Commission, on Tuesday challenged people in the party hostile to the European Union to declare whether they wanted Britain to leave the bloc.

"If those hostile to the European Union wish to pursue the debate with integrity, it is time for them to declare their hand," Brittan told a fringe meeting at the Conservative Party conference in Bournemouth.
He said he was sure that if the case for withdrawal was fully explored, the option would be conclusively rejected by the British people.
"Do they wish the UK to continue as a member of the European Union, or would they like to see Britain withdraw altogether?," Brittan asked of the Eurosceptics.
"If that is the case, the enormous costs of non-membership need to be set out so that a clear judgment can be made by the British people."
He added: "It is neither desirable nor honest to conduct a debate in which half the facts, but above all the underlying intentions, remain hidden."
He said it would be perverse for Britain to turn its back on Europe just as it was about to move in Britain's direction, becoming more diverse and less centralised as it expanded into Eastern Europe.
